blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Addresses with non-ASCII or percent-encoded characters reach the logs unmasked) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The pattern requires the character right before `@` to be ASCII and the domain to be ASCII, and needs a literal `@`. `logInfo("signup", { email: "josé@example.fr" })`, `"ada@exämple.de"` or a logged URL holding `ada%40example.org` match nothing and are written in full to the logs the hosting provider keeps 90 days — the very leak the change promises to stop (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 32). Match any non-space, non-`@` run around `@` (e.g. `/([^\s@<>"'])[^\s@<>"']*(?:@|%40)([^\s@<>"']+\.[^\s@<>"'.]{2,})/giu`) and add test cases for a Unicode local part, an IDN domain and a percent-encoded `@`.
findings.title: Addresses with non-ASCII or percent-encoded characters reach the logs unmasked

findings.recommendation: `a***@example.org` is still personal data when the domain is a small company or a personal domain: with the 90-day retention and the other fields of the log line, the customer can be re-identified (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25). Whether this matters depends on the customers' domains, which the reviewer could not see; if no log reader needs the domain, replace the whole address with a fixed token or a keyed hash, and ask the team whether the first letter and domain have a stated purpose.
findings.title: The masked form keeps the first letter and the full domain

findings.recommendation: Only the values pass through `maskEmails`; a field map keyed by address, such as `logInfo("quota", { [user.email]: 3 })`, writes the full address as a JSON key. Mask the key too (`safe[maskEmails(key)] = …`) so the module keeps its promise of never writing a full e-mail address.
findings.title: Field names are logged without masking
